name: fairy rath

attributes.attribute: circular earth wall raised by the Celts
held to be an opening to Fairyland
survived because it was not disturbed

sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 32–37.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy rath is a folkloric site. The Celts built circular earthen ramparts, known as raths or hillforts, to protect their hilltop palaces. Many of these stand still today. Folklore held such places to be openings to Fairyland, so they were off-limits to building. Fear of the punishment for meddling also covered such hallowed trees and mounds. Much of Ireland's oldest monuments survive because of these beliefs.
